solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: For some time wonder about rise being cut

indicators.note: about means one word is placed round the other, so the shortened rise sits within the wonder

parts.note: wonder means awe

indicators.note: being cut means the last letter of the rise is chopped off

parts.note: a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone marvels for a while about a slope that has been levelled off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean for a short period or a stretch of time.

clue.text: Initially when Harriet is running jewellery makes a vibratory noise

indicators.note: Initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Harriet goes for a run and her jewellery rattles and hums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word joining the wordplay to the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirring is a continuous buzzing or humming sound of rapid vibration.

clue.text: Inspired one judge to get into decent novel

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to get into means the judge's letter goes inside the rearranged word
novel means new, so the letters of decent are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge is moved to enter a respectable work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes NECTED from DECENT; 'to get into' puts J inside it after N, and I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired in the sense of breathed in or taken in, as a drug or fluid is introduced into the body.

clue.text: Sociable former girlfriend's some treasure! Right?

parts.note: an ex is a former girlfriend; the 's is the possessive in the surface only
a trove is a store of treasure, as in treasure trove

explanation.surface: Someone points out that an outgoing ex owns some treasure, and seeks agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, gregarious person is the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Dickens character runs into problem with it

indicators.note: into means the runs letter is placed inside the word for problem

parts.note: a catch is a hidden problem or snag
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the word it taken as written, with joining it to what goes before

explanation.surface: A Dickensian figure gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Cratchit is the underpaid clerk in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, a famous example of his characters.

clue.text: You're probably one of these brave critics with lust almost for upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters are overturned into a new order
almost means the final letter of lust is left off

explanation.surface: Bold reviewers with an appetite for causing upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LUST to LUS; 'upsetting' rearranges BRAVECRITICS with LUS. The definition speaks to you, the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword solvers and setters are fond of words; the reader of this clue is likely one of them.

clue.text: Greek hero accordingly besieges eastern borders of Syracuse

indicators.note: besieges means surrounds, so the first word goes round the others

parts.note: accordingly means thus

indicators.note: borders of means the first and last letters of the word Syracuse

explanation.surface: A Greek hero lays siege to the edges of the Sicilian city of Syracuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian who slew the Minotaur is a legendary figure of Greek myth.

clue.text: Drink in mixture

parts.note: being in means being at home
a brew is a mixture, as of drink or ideas

explanation.surface: A drink served in a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it gives HOME, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer or wine made at your own house is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Number refuse to accept Catholic inclination

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the Catholic letter goes inside

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

explanation.surface: Some people decline to take on a Catholic leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a leaning or disposition towards something.

clue.text: I just shuffled behind odd characters to join up for martial art

indicators.note: behind means the rearranged letters come after the picked ones
odd characters are the first, third and fifth letters of join up
shuffled means the letters of I just are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone moves aside to join a martial arts class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' looks like a dance step but signals the anagram; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jujitsu is a Japanese system of unarmed combat, a fighting discipline.

clue.text: Language not quite relevant

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: germane means relevant

explanation.surface: Wording that misses the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final E of GERMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Germany and Austria is a language.

clue.text: Croc wallowing in black oil that's obscured greens

indicators.note: in means the tumbled croc goes inside the black letter and disguised oil

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: obscured means disguised, so the letters of oil are hidden in a new order
wallowing means rolling about, so the letters of croc are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A crocodile rolls about in a black slick that hides the vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'wallowing' works on CROC and 'that's obscured' on OIL; 'greens' turns from colour to vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable, and greens are leafy vegetables in general.

clue.text: Argument about hollow life is unconvincing

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a beef is a complaint or argument

indicators.note: hollow means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of life

explanation.surface: A dispute over an empty existence is unpersuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BEEF into FEEB; 'hollow' leaves LE from LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak or lame excuse is one that fails to persuade.

clue.text: Nitrogen and oxygen, e.g., make the weather

definitions.meaning: nitrogen and oxygen are examples of chemical substances in the periodic table
exposure to the ... means exposure to wind and rain

explanation.surface: The gases in the air determine the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical substances on the periodic table, and also the forces of wind, rain and cold.

clue.text: Spooner's dog advice cheers

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: a poodle is a dog
a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A cheery farewell offered as canine advice.
explanation.walkthrough: POODLE TIP with its opening letters swapped becomes the old-fashioned British farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Old artist returns without son

indicators.note: without means the son letter is taken away
returns means the artist's name is read backwards

parts.note: Degas was a French painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter comes back without his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DEGAS into SAGED; 'without' removes the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone advanced in years, elderly.

clue.text: Designed pan shot through with carbon, gold and copper as receptacle for fruit

indicators.note: designed means arranged, so the letters of pan are set out anew
shot through with says the chemical and heraldic letters are worked in among the rearranged pan letters

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
OR is gold in heraldry
CU is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A crafted pan streaked with carbon, gold and copper holds fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pan's letters come out as A..N..P, with COR and CU threaded between them; OR is heraldic gold, CU the symbol for copper. 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The cup-shaped base holding an acorn is the fruit's receptacle on the oak.

clue.text: Proof of empty dialogue in show

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the word for show

parts.note: to evince is to show or display

indicators.note: empty means the inside of dialogue is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A display of hollow conversation proves something.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the information that establishes a fact, the proof of something.

clue.text: A wide track turning to one side

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wide
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A broad path that bends off to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is out of line, twisted away to one side.

clue.text: Could it prevent a sort of tainted love being embraced?

indicators.note: being embraced means the love letter is held inside the rearranged word
a sort of means a variant, so the letters of tainted are sorted into a new order

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether something might stop love going bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges TAINTED to ANTIDTE; 'being embraced' puts O inside it. The clue nods to the song Tainted Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy counteracts a poison, so it might prevent its effects.

clue.text: Objection put in afterwards, mounting argument against

indicators.note: put in means the objection goes inside the word for afterwards
mounting in a down clue means going up, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: later means afterwards
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: An objection lodged later, building a case against.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounting' means read upwards, so backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument refuting a claim.

clue.text: Rigid small boat in Loire, good for going around river

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: going around means the French word surrounds the river letter

parts.note: bon is French for good, as spoken in the Loire valley

explanation.surface: A stiff little boat on the Loire circles a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate, unbending, refusing to change.

clue.text: African people sail with storms when temperature's dropped

indicators.note: storms means rages, so the letters of sail with are thrown about
dropped means the temperature letter is taken out

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Sailors from Africa set out in stormy weather once the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' rearranges SAILWITH; 'dropped' removes the T; 'when' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swahili are a Bantu people of the East African coast.

clue.text: MP gets the bird!

definitions.meaning: MP is military police; a British military policeman is so called from his ... cover
a name used for the goldfinch and other birds with red heads

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament is booed or jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' means is jeered; but MP is the military police, not a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a British military policeman and a red-headed bird such as the goldfinch go by this name.

clue.text: Flower, say, planted in imaginary land

indicators.note: say signals that the flower's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the lily is a flower
to plant is to put or place something

explanation.surface: A flower set in the ground in a fantasy country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a lily, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's island of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels is a fictional country.

clue.text: Frank is caught with papers

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
and means with, joining things together
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is arrested carrying his documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank both mean open, honest and outspoken.

clue.text: Tees backs up

definitions.meaning: golf tees are pegs that hold up the ball
backs up means stands behind or bolsters

explanation.definitionFit: Golf tees hold balls up, and to back someone up is to bolster them.

clue.text: Cherished abstract housed in Oxford University. Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: housed in signals one word placed inside another
Quite the opposite reverses the stated order, so the university goes inside the summary

parts.note: a precis is an abstract or summary

explanation.surface: A treasured summary is kept at Oxford, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the summary would sit inside the university; 'Quite the opposite' flips which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precious is dearly loved and held dear.

clue.text: Make stew from leg bone? There's no time

indicators.note: There's no means the time letter is removed

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap, a bone in the leg

explanation.surface: A cook in a hurry makes a stew from a leg bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' and 'from' are link words; 'There's no' removes T from PATELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish rice dish of saffron, seafood and meat is a kind of stew.
